Package hadur2.core

Class HadurCore

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.HadurCore
public final class HadurCore extends Object
Hadur's brain. One instance lives for a whole battle; tick(hadur2.core.model.BotInput) turns each BotInput into BotOrders. It never touches the Robocode API (CORE-1) and holds no randomness, threads, reflection or I/O (RES-6), so the same inputs always give the same orders (CORE-2).

Per tick it handles the tick's events first, then runs the main loop body, the same order in which Robocode runs event handlers and then run().

The PostureGate picks the subsystems each tick, failing closed to the duel: the MeleeController drives while two or more opponents are alive, no sentry is on the field or has been scanned this round, and melee has not thrown this round (GATE-1 to GATE-4). Once one opponent is left, the duel machinery below takes over from a clean slate (MELEE-2). When the duel drives with several opponents alive it fights one, the DuelFocus, and ignores the rest; with sentries about, the SentryFence keeps its movement out of their border. Sentries are never tracked, targeted or profiled (GATE-5). The melee extension adds this routing and leaves the duel's packages untouched.

In a duel with a ProfileStore, the first scan loads the opponent's profile (MEM-1), each round's observations are folded into it when the round ends (MEM-2), and saveProfile(long) persists it (MEM-3). Melee battles never write a 1v1 profile. They keep a melee block per opponent instead (MeleeMemory): loaded on the opponent's first scan, folded when the round ends and written by saveProfile(long) (MMEM-1).

When a melee's opponents fall to one, the survivor's first scan hands it to the duel (MMEM-2): the shots the melee saw it fire that are still short of Hadur become the duel's firing waves, and its 1v1 profile, read but never written, sets the duel's opening (the surf's prior, the starting distance, the movement's baseline and POW-1's gun tier). An H record says what was handed over.

The loaded profile also decides the battle's opening (S4): the OpeningBook reads its tiers once and picks the first gun (ADAPT-1) and the surf's prior (ADAPT-2), and its seeds are replayed into the KNN views at half a live sample's weight over the next ticks (ADAPT-3). Each wave then checks the live estimates against the profile's, and a seed the opponent no longer matches fades out (RES-4). A stranger, or a profile too thin to trust, opens exactly as 1.20 did (DIAL-1).

S5 makes it aggressive. The DistancePolicy starts at the opening's distance and moves a step a wave on the gap between the rolling hit rates (DIST-1); the PowerPolicy fires full power against a gun that cannot hit us (POW-1, POW-2); and the Endgame closes in to finish a weak enemy (END-1) and rams a disabled one (END-2).

S6 makes it harder to hit and keeps it inside its turn: each of our bullets in flight shadows part of the enemy's waves (MOVE-1), the movement changes flavour when their gun beats its profile (MOVE-2), and the TickBudget sheds work after a slow tick or a skipped turn (TIME-1, TIME-2). Against a bullet shielder the ShieldDetector and AimJitter move each shot's aim off the predictable line (SHIELD-1, SHIELD-2).

One tick(hadur2.core.model.BotInput), in order:

  1. Sentry scans are reported to the gate, which then picks this tick's Posture from the opponent and sentry counts (GATE-1 to GATE-3). If melee has just ended, the duel's tracking is reset and full speed restored before any scan is handled (MELEE-2).
  2. The tick's events, in the order the adapter queued them (the engine's own). Every non-sentry scan updates the melee tracker; in the duel posture the scan of the duel's opponent also logs both robots' states, creates a gun wave and a movement wave, and runs the energy ledger (WAVE-1, WAVE-2). Bullet and collision events feed the ledger, the hit windows, the shield detector and the shadows; TickTime and SkippedTurn feed the tick budget.
  3. In a duel, a few seed samples are replayed into the KNN views (ADAPT-3).
  4. The driving posture's main body. Melee: fire last tick's aim if the gun got there, then ask the MeleeController for radar, destination and aim. Duel: fire and aim, break the movement's waves, check the seeds (RES-4), step the distance and endgame policies, update the shadows, surf (or ram), and sweep the radar if the enemy was lost (RADAR-1). Before the duel's first scan it only spins the radar.
  5. With sentries on the field, the duel's orders pass through the SentryFence (GATE-3).

Units and conventions follow Robocode: positions in px with x growing east and y north, angles in radians with headings absolute (0 = north, clockwise) and bearings relative to our heading, time in ticks, energy and bullet power in the engine's units. A wave's guess factor is in [-1, 1], the fraction of the maximum escape angle on the side the target was moving. The core writes line records to Telemetry: V (once, when the core is made), B (battle and opponent, at the first duel scan), P (a policy decision), EW (an enemy wave the ledger found), MEM (a memory failure), FAULT, R (round end, see RoundStats) and M (the melee extension's round end).

Nothing grows without bound (RES-2): the subsystems cap their own logs, trees and windows, and the only collection held here, the round's dead robots, stops at 64 names.

  • Method Details

    • newRound

      public void newRound(int round)
      Starts a round. Transient state (waves, logs, the melee tracker, the gate's veto, the tick budget's round level) is cleared; what was learned (KNN views, virtual-gun ratings, the profile, the hit windows, the distance controller, the shield verdict) carries on, because the core lives for the whole battle.
      Parameters:
      round - the round number, from 0

    • recover

      public void recover()
      Forgets this round's transient state (waves, logs, the last scan) but keeps everything learned. Used after a fault, so a bad state can't fault every tick.

    • roundEnded

      public RoundStats roundEnded(long tick, String result, double myEnergy, int faults)
      Emits the round-end record and returns this round's statistics. result is win, loss or draw; faults is the number of ticks the Guard had to cover for this round.

      Also folds the round into the opponent's profile (MEM-2) and copies the memory library's battle totals into the record (MEM-3 to MEM-5, RES-5). A battle with several opponents, or with sentries, gets an M record as well.

      Parameters:
      tick - the tick the round ended on
      result - win, loss or draw
      myEnergy - our energy at the round's end
      faults - ticks the guard covered this round
      Returns:
      this round's statistics, complete

    • meleeRecord

      String meleeRecord(long tick)
      The melee extension's round record, for battles with several opponents or sentries: M,round,tick,meleeTicks,duelTicks,focusTicks,veto,meleeFaults,maxScanGap, ghostTicks,sentryHits,sweepGap,ghostsDropped,wavesSent,wavesResolved,virtualHits, memFailures; the wave counts are the round's targeting waves (MGUN-4) and how many the field gun's aim would have hit. The veto is -, sentry or fault; sentryHits counts our bullets that hit a sentry. M5 appends memFailures, the battle's melee memory failures so far (RES-5). Fields are only ever appended.

    • saveProfile

      public void saveProfile(long tick)
      MEM-3: writes the profile to the store in full, seeds included. The adapter calls this when the battle ends; round-end checkpoints while the battle continues go through checkpoint(long) instead (TIME-4), which only writes seeds on every tenth one. Does nothing when the battle keeps no memory. In a melee battle it writes the melee blocks instead (MMEM-1); the adapter only checkpoints while Hadur is alive, so a round Hadur died in is written at the next checkpoint or at the battle's end.

      The library does the atomic write (RES-3) and any eviction (MEM-5) and never throws; anything but a clean write is logged as a MEM record.

      Parameters:
      tick - the tick of the save, for the record

    • checkpoint

      public void checkpoint(long tick)
      TIME-4: a round-end checkpoint. Every checkpoint writes the profile's statistics; only every tenth one also writes its seeds, so a battle of hundreds of rounds does not spend its whole data quota on checkpoints nobody but the last one needs. The final save at the battle's end (battleEnded(long)) always writes the seeds.
      Parameters:
      tick - the tick of the save, for the record
